note: Re-judged 2026-11-14 at 5d862bbab9 by an independent auditor who authored none of the changes named. RFC 8654 Section 5: "A BGP speaker that has the ability to use BGP Extended Messages but has not advertised the BGP Extended Message Capability, presumably due to configuration, MUST NOT accept a BGP Extended Message." One cited producer moved: Session.negotiateWith gained one statement, s.negotiatedPeerAS.Store(negotiated.PeerASN), placed under writeMu beside the store of s.negotiated, so a sent-event callback (Reactor.notifyOneMessage through negotiatedPeerASNoWait) can name a dynamic peer's AS without the session lock. It reads a field capability.Negotiate already returned and writes an atomic no receive path reads. The lines this row cites negotiateWith for are untouched: the call to capability.Negotiate, where ExtendedMessageRecv is set from the local advertisement alone, and s.extendedMessage = s.negotiated.ExtendedMessageRecv, the receive permission both readers hand to Header.ValidateLengthWithMax; writeBuf.Resize still follows ExtendedMessageSend, the peer's advertisement, which is the send side and Section 4. The check names no other moved unit. Of the tagged units I re-read TestRFC8654ReceiveLimitFollowsLocalOPEN, byte-identical to the recorded one: it runs the real OPEN exchange for the four advertisement combinations, both readers, at 4096, 4097 and 65535 octets, and requires for local=false above 4096 an error, zero dispatch and a NOTIFICATION 1/2 whose data is the offending Length, and for accepted input one intact dispatch, Established and no bytes answered. It goes through negotiateWith, so it fails if the receive permission followed the peer's capability. The judgement of TestValidateLengthWithMax and of the two FRR interop checkers stands as recorded and was not re-read. Source audit only; no test, record or interop run was made for this rejudgment. Verdict unchanged: enforced.
